parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$v=(-k/-0.5)t^{-1/2}+d=2kt^{-1/2}+d$ [*M1: integration; no need for constant; allow given $k=2.6$; power increases by 1 with coefficient change; use of $v=at$ scores M0].

$\text{their }1.6=2k(4^{-1/2})+d=k+d$ and $0.3=2k(16^{-1/2})+d=k/2+d$ [A1 FT: both equations in $k,d$; allow unsimplified].

Attempt to solve for $k$ or $d$ [DM1; alternatively substitute $k=2.6$ into both and solve both for non-zero $d$; must reach $k=$ or $d=$].

$k=2.6$, $v=5.2t^{-1/2}-1$ (or $v=(-2.6/-0.5)t^{-1/2}-1$) [A1 AG for $k$, not expression; allow unsimplified/in $k$; if $k$ substituted, both equations must show $d=-1$ and yield the expression; SC B1 for solving correct equations with no work and correct $v$; SC A1 for correct $v$ if only first M1 scored].

Alternative using limits: same integration [*M1]; $(-k/-0.5)4^{-1/2}-(-k/-0.5)16^{-1/2}=1.6-0.3$, or $2k4^{-1/2}-2k16^{-1/2}=1.6-0.3$ [A1 FT OE: correct unsimplified equation using limits $4,16$ and velocities their $1.6,0.3$]; attempt solve for $k$ [DM1: equation using $0.3$, their $k$, $16,4$, subtracting limits; sign errors allowed in $1.6-0.3$]; $k=2.6$, $v=5.2t^{-1/2}-1$ [A1 AG for $k$, not expression; allow unsimplified/in $k$]. Total: 4.

parts.label: (d)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$\int_0^4 0.2t^{3/2}\,dt=(0.2/2.5)t^{5/2}$ or $\int_4^{27.04}(5.2t^{-1/2}-\text{their }1)\,dt=(5.2/0.5)t^{1/2}-\text{their }1\,t$ [M1: integration of the stated velocity forms; may be in $k$; not another expression; their constant may be zero; may come from (b) or (c); power must increase by 1 with coefficient change in at least one term].

$[(0.2/2.5)t^{5/2}]_0^4+[(5.2/0.5)t^{1/2}-t]_4^{27.04}$, or $[0.08t^{5/2}]_0^4+[10.4t^{1/2}-t]_4^{27.04}$ [A1ft: both unsimplified integrals; limits not required; FT non-zero $d$, possibly in $k$; the official guidance says “Their 1 may came from either part (b) or part (c)”—the grammatical anomaly is retained as printed].

$0.08(32)+(10.4(5.2)-27.04)-(10.4(2)-4)=2.56+10.24$ [M1: correct use of limits $0,4$ then $4$, their $27.04$ in both integrals from the stated velocity forms; their constant may be zero; allow M1 for $d=0$, giving final $35.8$].

$64/5$ or $12.8$ [A1 OE, AWRT $12.8$; allow $27(.0)$ instead of $27.04$; allow all four marks if the Q7(b) velocity expression is correct, however obtained].

SC for calculator integration: either $\int_0^4 0.2t^{3/2}\,dt=2.56$, or $\int_4^{27.04}(5.2t^{-1/2}-1)\,dt=10.24$ [B1 for either result; AWRT $2.56$ for the first; allow $10.2$ for the second; must use $27.04$ or $27(.0)$ for the latter]; total distance $=12.8\,\mathrm{m}$ [B1 AWRT; allow $27(.0)$; allow both B marks if the Q7(b) velocity expression is correct]. Total: 4.
